fact: Penn Today reports Sierra Leone's government scaled a machine-learning medicine demand forecasting and allocation tool nationwide, now supporting over 70 products, with ownership fully transferred to the government.
Penn Today reports a pilot in five districts found a 19% increase in consumption of allocated medical products in treated areas, published in Nature.

A pilot launched in 2022 in Tonkolili district integrates BabyChecker AI ultrasound into routine antenatal visits, with free scans and risk-based referrals, per a White Ribbon Alliance study presented in 2024.
